newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BMW Belgium sets 3.0 bln Bfr CP programme.
newsitem.headline: BMW Belgium sets 3.0 bln Bfr CP programme.

text.p: BMW Belgium, a fully-owned subsidiary of BMW AG, has set up a commercial paper programme for a maximum of three billion Belgian francs or its equivalent in any other freely available foreign currency, arranging bank Generale Bank said on Friday.
Generale Bank said in a statement the paper will be issued in dematerialised form and have maturities of at least 15 days.
It said BMW Belgium plans to use the proceeds for regular operations.
Generale Bank will also act as dealer, together with Kredietbank, and also act as domiciliary agent for the issuer.
Founded in 1974 BMW Belgium sells BMW cars, motorcycles and spare parts and handles after-sales maintenance.
BMW's market share in Belgium increased to 4.1 percent in the first half of 1996 from 2.3 percent in 1990, the statement said.
It said BMW Belgium forecast 1996 sales volume of 16,000 new cars, 1,400 motorcycles and turnover of 1.9 billion Belgian francs in spare parts. Total turnover is expected to reach 17 billion francs.
BMW Belgium is forecasting five percent average annual growth in the period to the year 2002, Generale Bank said.
